** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Qualify the float32 model claim.**

On CUDA, the default detector uses half-precision autocast even with float32 weights. The first logit interpolation now runs in float32 instead of half precision, so its outputs can change. Qualify “Float32 models are unchanged” to exclude this path. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kornia/kornia/42bc48f10bc63bd941985d79e2f80b65027d6102/kornia/feature/dedode/decoder.py))

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Skip the unsupported MPS/float64 test cases.**

When the fixtures select MPS and float64, `.to(device, dtype)` fails before this attention test reaches its assertion. The new dropout test and `test_detector_returns_at_least_float32_logits` have the same failure. Add an explicit skip to each test that allocates float64 tensors on MPS. The fixtures include this combination, and PyTorch does not support it. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kornia/kornia/42bc48f10bc63bd941985d79e2f80b65027d6102/conftest.py))

As per coding guidelines, “Never create `float64` tensors on the device in non-gradcheck tests”; skip explicitly when double precision is unsupported.
